Django 5.1.

Let me know if there's a better forum for this discussion. Happy to post elsewhere, but I thought it might be relevant to this PR.

I've upgraded to `v5.1b1` locally and tried out these changes, and it still doesn't seem to be resolving this pooling issue for me. I'm using the Django ORM with a Gunicorn ASGI server + Uvicorn workers. I see that the number of my open connections to the server seems to uniformly increase. I'm testing this on PostgreSQL 15.5, arm64. Any help or consultation would be much appreciated. You can also reach me at saba at khoj.dev.

This is my configuration. I've also tried playing with `CONN_MAX_AGE`:

```
DATABASES = {
    "default": {
        "ENGINE": "django.db.backends.postgresql",
        "HOST": os.getenv("POSTGRES_HOST", "localhost"),
        "PORT": os.getenv("POSTGRES_PORT", "5432"),
        "USER": os.getenv("POSTGRES_USER", "postgres"),
        "NAME": os.getenv("POSTGRES_DB", "khoj"),
        "PASSWORD": os.getenv("POSTGRES_PASSWORD", "postgres"),
        "CONN_MAX_AGE": 0,
        "CONN_HEALTH_CHECKS": True,
        },
        "OPTIONS": {
            "default_transaction_isolation": "read committed",
            "client_encoding": "UTF8",
            "timezone": "UTC",
            "pool": True,
        }
}
```

Our setup is a little bespoke, so the issue could be niche. We're using FastAPI for our API layer. [See GitHub repo](https://github.com/khoj-ai/khoj).

## New Info

EDIT: I realized there was an error in `OPTIONS` configuration. Fixed to this:
```
    "default": {
        "ENGINE": "django.db.backends.postgresql",
        "HOST": os.getenv("POSTGRES_HOST", "localhost"),
        "PORT": os.getenv("POSTGRES_PORT", "5432"),
        "USER": os.getenv("POSTGRES_USER", "postgres"),
        "NAME": os.getenv("POSTGRES_DB", "khoj"),
        "PASSWORD": os.getenv("POSTGRES_PASSWORD", "postgres"),
        "CONN_MAX_AGE": 0,
        "CONN_HEALTH_CHECKS": True,
        "OPTIONS": {
            "pool": True,
        }
    },
```

Which results in some connection errors, `django.db.utils.OperationalError: couldn't get a connection after 30.00 sec`. It connects at first, and the connections are stable at 4. After a few queries, the error above starts popping up. I also had to remove the other values under `OPTIONS` for the application to start up. Maybe subsequent queries aren't pulling from the pool appropriately?

## Newer Info

In case anyone comes across this, our issue seems to stem from our custom setup. Because we're using FastAPI as our API layer, I think Django wasn't able to close out the DB sessions properly as each of them use different threads (`thread.local` vs `contextvars`). 

We ended up using some solutions discussed in this thread: https://github.com/tiangolo/fastapi/discussions/8009. This has mitigated the problem for now.

Note the connection pooling within Django still doesn't work, but manually forcing all the open sessions to close from the respective threads seems to be a decent stop gap. See relevant commit here: https://github.com/khoj-ai/khoj/commit/4471c1e37fdf09d7c8bd20a9e35f29bc72b7dead.

@sabaimran Could explain why connection pooling still doesn't work after this PR? I'd hazard a guess that this PR should fix everything.
Context: We're planning a django upgrade from 3.2 to 5.1 and we use a lot of different databases and connection pools. I'm planning the upgrade for async views support and I need to know if there would be any potential issues, so I'd be grateful for your answer here.
Please discuss this in a new issue, not here.

Hi 👋

How does the connection pooling interact with CONN_MAX_AGE? I couldn't find anything about this in the [docs](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/5.1/ref/databases/#connection-pool)

Do you by default propagate it into [ConnectionPool](https://www.psycopg.org/psycopg3/docs/api/pool.html#psycopg_pool.ConnectionPool) `max_lifetime` kwarg by any chance?

Notably, what happens if we set CONN_MAX_AGE=None (persistent connections)? We're running pgbouncer with pool_mode `session` rather than pool_mode `transaction` because of migrations.

This answer suggests pool_mode `transaction` with CONN_MAX_AGE=None: https://stackoverflow.com/a/35473402/5511061 but we're looking to keep pool_mode `session` and adopt this PR with optimal settings.

Any tips are appreciated!
@ddelange This question would be better asked on the [forum](https://forum.djangoproject.com/) or Discord, rather than the original implementation PR.
fyi I've opened https://github.com/django/django/pull/19442 to address the above in the docs 👍

issue.title: Support connection pooling kwargs

repository.name: dj-database-url
repository.description: Use Database URLs in your Django Application.

issue.body:
Hi 👋

We would like to migrate to dj-database-url (more precisely [`environs[django]`](https://pypi.org/project/environs/)), but we are currently leveraging the psycopg v3 database [connection pool](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/5.1/ref/databases/#connection-pool) functionality (new in django v5.1).

Is there a generic mechanic in place to migrate the following code to the dj-database-url `parse` constructor?

```py
"OPTIONS": {
    # TODO replace with ?sslmode=require in DATABASE_URL
    "sslmode": env("DJANGO_DB_SSLMODE", "require"),
    # https://www.psycopg.org/psycopg3/docs/api/pool.html#psycopg_pool.ConnectionPool    
    "pool": {
        "min_size": env.int("DJANGO_DB_POOL_MIN_SIZE", 4),
        "max_size": env.int("DJANGO_DB_POOL_MAX_SIZE", 32),
        "max_lifetime": env.int("CONN_MAX_AGE", 60 * 60),
        "max_idle": env.int("CONN_MAX_IDLE", 10 * 60),
    },
},
```

issue.title: Add psycopg connection pool metrics and configurability
issue.body:
## Summary

Adds comprehensive PostgreSQL connection pool monitoring and configuration for production deployments. Introduces a Prometheus metrics collector for psycopg_pool statistics, environment-based pool configuration with sensible defaults, and extensive test coverage for pool settings.

## Key Changes

- **New `db_pool_metrics.py` module**: Prometheus collector that exports psycopg_pool statistics (pool size, available connections, request queues, timeouts, etc.) as metrics on the `/metrics` endpoint. Gracefully handles missing pools and errors to avoid impacting app startup or metrics scraping.

- **Pool configuration in `settings.py`**: 
  - Added `_env_flag()` helper for parsing boolean environment variables (accepts "1", "true", "yes", "on")
  - Implemented opt-in connection pooling via `PG_USE_POOL` flag with sensible defaults:
    - `PG_POOL_MIN_SIZE` (default: 2)
    - `PG_POOL_MAX_SIZE` (default: 16, auto-grows to min_size if needed)
    - `PG_POOL_TIMEOUT` (default: 5s, fail-fast on starvation)
    - `PG_POOL_MAX_WAITING` (default: 2×max_size, bounds the waiter queue)
    - `PG_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` (default: 10s, clamped to libpq minimum of 2s)
  - Pool is disabled by default to avoid connection starvation issues from executor threads that never return checkouts
  - Added `CONN_HEALTH_CHECKS=True` when pooling is enabled for transparent failover recovery

- **New `apps.py`**: Django AppConfig that registers the pool metrics collector at startup via `ready()` hook

- **Comprehensive test coverage**:
  - `test_db_pool_metrics.py`: Unit tests for the collector (describe/collect behavior, error handling, unopened pool skipping)
  - `test_prod_database_settings.py`: Integration tests for pool configuration (defaults, env overrides, clamping, malformed values)

- **Documentation updates**:
  - Updated `k8s/db-host-configurability.md` to reflect removal of stale `-back` deployment files
  - Created `k8s/uploads-pvc.yaml` as the manifest of record for the shared uploads PVC (previously embedded in deleted deploy-back.yaml)
  - Updated `k8s/temporal/worker.yaml` and `k8s/temporal/README.md` to reference the new PVC manifest

- **Removed stale Kubernetes manifests**: Deleted `k8s/deploy-back.yaml` and `k8s/deploy_staging-back.yaml` (backup copies no longer applied by the deploy pipeline)

## Implementation Details

The pool metrics collector uses a two-phase approach:
- `describe()` returns static metric families from configuration tables (safe during AppConfig.ready() before Django's app registry is fully initialized)
- `collect()` lazily imports django.db.connections and iterates pools, gracefully skipping misconfigured aliases and unopened pools

Pool configuration is designed to prevent the starvation incidents that caused 60s ingress 504s: the default max_size of 16 accommodates the legitimate concurrent ORM users in a web worker (sync lane + executors), and the fail-fast timeout prevents cascading waiter stalls. Pooling remains opt-in pending proof of thread connection hygiene.
